title: EMBridge: Enhancing Gesture Generalization from EMG Signals Through Cross-modal Representation Learning
claim: Unimodal embeddings from weak signals are entangled while a richer modality is well structured, so we align the weak one to it.
layout: 2 panels, left motivation and right architecture, left-to-right flow with feedback arrows
description: Two framed panels sit side by side. Panel (a), titled 'Why Cross-Modal Learning', has two rows. The top row takes an EMG waveform through an EMG-MAE encoder to a messy, diffuse scatter of embeddings, labeled 'Diffuse/Entangled'. The bottom row takes hand pose images through a Pose-MAE encoder to a clustered, color-separated scatter, labeled 'Structured' and 'Discriminative'. A vertical 'Align' arrow links the two rows. Panel (b), titled 'EMBridge', is a block diagram. An EMG encoder, shown with a flame icon, feeds K,V into cross-attention. Learnable queries and masked pose tokens enter a self-attention block. Further blocks (feed-forward, decoding layer) lead to the Contrastive Learning and Masked Pose Reconstruction losses. A frozen pose encoder, shown with a snowflake icon, supplies targets. Pastel boxes and yellow loss boxes carry the color coding.
caption: (a) Motivation for cross-modal representation learning: using the same MAE pre-training, pose embeddings are semantically structured and well-separated across gestures (colors), whereas EMG embeddings are not. This motivates leveraging pose as guidance to structure the EMG representation space. (b) Detailed architecture of EMBridge. Only one transformer block (self-attention, cross-attention, and feed-forward layers) is shown for clarity, the model uses four such blocks.
abstract: Hand gesture classification using high-quality structured data such as videos, images, and hand skeletons is a well-explored problem in computer vision. Alternatively, leveraging low-power, cost-effective bio-signals, e.g. surface electromyography (sEMG), allows for continuous gesture prediction on wearable devices. In this work, we aim to enhance EMG representation quality by aligning it with embeddings obtained from structured, high-quality modalities that provide richer semantic guidance, ultimately enabling zero-shot gesture generalization. Specifically, we propose EMBridge, a cross-modal representation learning framework that bridges the modality gap between EMG and pose. EMBridge learns high-quality EMG representations by introducing a Querying Transformer (Q-Former), a masked pose reconstruction loss, and a community-aware soft contrastive learning objective that aligns the relative geometry of the embedding spaces. We evaluate EMBridge on both in-distribution and unseen gesture classification tasks and demonstrate consistent performance gains over all baselines. To the best of our knowledge, EMBridge is the first cross-modal representation learning framework to achieve zero-shot gesture classification from wearable EMG signals, showing potential toward real-world gesture recognition on wearable devices.
